title: Wikipedia Maliciously Tampered With, Google Incorrectly Reports Death of OpenAI CEO Altman

content_html:
On Wednesday morning local time, some X and Reddit users discovered that searching for the name of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on Google resulted in a search result indicating that he had died that day. A few hours later, Google admitted that the search result was incorrect and responded on X: "The information is no longer displayed. This was not a manual modification by Google. When someone maliciously alters public information sources, it may affect the information displayed in the search results."

Netizens generally speculated that this was related to the malicious tampering of Wikipedia. The revision history of Sam Altman's Wikipedia page showed unusually frequent activity on that day, with 22 edits made in just one day, while the page had only been updated five times since the beginning of the month, and each update occurred on different dates.

"Death Announcement" to "Name Change": A Malicious Operation Lasting Several Hours

The timeline of the incident reveals the farce: at 9:47 AM Coordinated Universal Time, the page was modified to show false information stating that Altman was assassinated on Wednesday; at 10:29 AM, the content was corrected. However, the page then underwent a series of modifications, including adding a description that Altman was a "dropout," reasserting his death, and even maliciously changing his surname from "Altman" to "Gayman." As of the time of this report, the latest update seems to have corrected all previous errors, but this malicious editing still exposed a vulnerable aspect of the search ecosystem.

The core controversy of this incident lies in Google's Knowledge Panel. As an information area displayed at the top of some search results, the content of the Knowledge Panel comes from various public information sources, with Wikipedia being one of the most frequently cited. Google previously explained that its information comes from hundreds of sources across the internet, not solely relying on Wikipedia, and has an information reporting mechanism where users can flag incorrect information, and once policy violations are identified, "it will be manually removed." However, this incident shows that in the AI era, increasingly reliant on real-time information retrieval, a publicly edited encyclopedia page being maliciously rewritten is sufficient to contaminate search results and create large-scale rumors within a short period of time. How to build a stronger defense between the massive amount of public information and content credibility remains a long-term challenge for platforms like Google.

content_html_zh:
当地时间周三上午，一些 X 和 Reddit 用户发现，在 Google 上搜索 OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 的名字，结果显示搜索结果显示他当天去世。 几个小时后，谷歌承认搜索结果不正确，并在X上回应：“该信息不再显示。 这不是 Google 手动修改的。 当有人恶意更改公共信息来源时，可能会影响搜索结果中显示的信息。”

网友普遍猜测这与维基百科被恶意篡改有关。 萨姆·奥尔特曼的维基百科页面的修订历史显示，当天的活动异常频繁，仅一天之内就进行了 22 次编辑，而该页面自本月初以来仅更新了 5 次，而且每次更新都发生在不同的日期。

“死亡公告”到“更名”：持续数小时的恶意操作

该事件的时间线揭示了这场闹剧：协调世界时间上午9点47分，该页面被修改以显示虚假信息，声称奥特曼于周三被暗杀；上午10点29分，内容已更正。 然而，该页面随后经历了一系列修改，包括添加奥特曼是“辍学生”的描述、重申他的死亡，甚至恶意将他的姓氏从“奥特曼”改为“盖曼”。 截至本报告发布时，最新的更新似乎已经纠正了之前的所有错误，但这种恶意编辑仍然暴露了搜索生态系统的一个脆弱方面。

此次事件的核心争议在于谷歌的知识面板。 作为一些搜索结果顶部显示的信息区域，知识面板的内容来自各种公共信息源，其中维基百科是最常被引用的之一。 谷歌此前解释称，其信息来自互联网上数百个来源，不仅仅依赖维基百科，并且拥有信息报告机制，用户可以标记不正确的信息，一旦发现违反政策的行为，“将被手动删除”。 然而，这起事件表明，在越来越依赖实时信息检索的人工智能时代，一个公开编辑的百科全书页面被恶意重写，足以在短时间内污染搜索结果并制造大规模谣言。 如何在海量的公共信息和内容可信度之间建立更强有力的防御，仍然是谷歌等平台面临的长期挑战。
